title: Provider Egress Policy
description: XP-03: tier x provider egress gate for the delegation face (a task contract / context pack handed to an external LLM CLI), as opposed to egress-policy.json (SA-04, network/domain face). Declares, per provider, whether inference stays on this machine (local-only) or is sent to a vendor API (external-api) and, when it is sent, whether the vendor uses that material to train models. Tiers above confidential are never sent off the machine; confidential may be sent only to a provider whose material is not trained on. Consumed by libs/core/provider-egress-gate.ts's checkProviderEgress.

providers.description: Egress and training-use declaration per provider id. A provider absent from this map is treated as unknown -- not automatically local-only.

egress.description: 'external-api': the provider's CLI sends the payload to a vendor-hosted API. 'local-only': inference stays on this machine.

training_use.description: Whether the vendor uses material sent to this provider to train models. 'none': contractually not trained on. 'used': trained on. 'unknown': not established -- treated as 'used' by the gate, so an undeclared provider fails closed. The same API can differ by plan, so declare `plan` alongside this.

plan.description: The account or plan this declaration applies to (e.g. 'api-paid', 'free-tier'). The same provider id can have different training-use terms per plan; this records which one is configured here.

basis.description: Where the training_use claim was verified -- a terms URL, contract reference or ticket. A 'none' claim with no basis is an assertion, not a fact.

tier_policy.description: Per data tier, which providers may receive material of that tier. `public` is always any-provider and is not overridable here -- the gate fails open for public regardless of this file's presence/validity.

approved_providers.description: Provider ids allowed to receive confidential material regardless of their declared training use. Every entry here is an operator exception that the coverage report names, not a derived approval.

confidential.description: Confidential material may leave the machine only for a provider declared `training_use: none`. `approved_providers` remains as an explicit, audited operator exception for providers that are not (yet) declared so.

approved_providers.description: Provider ids allowed to receive personal material regardless of their declared training use. Every entry is an operator exception that fails no gate but is named in reports.

personal.description: Personal material may leave the machine only for a provider that does not train on it -- the same bar as confidential. Keeping it on the machine is one way to satisfy that, not a separate requirement: personal work has real uses (trip research, say) that need a model, and a rule that forbids them is a rule that gets bypassed.

attestation_ttl_days.description: How long a tenant provider attestation stays valid without an explicit expires_at. A plan can be downgraded and vendor terms can change without anyone touching this repository, so a claim that is never re-verified must decay to 'unknown' rather than hold forever.
